newEntriesNeeded.title: DbView sub-object types: ELEL, EXPFIL, ATTFIL, EXPCOL, ATTCOL
newEntriesNeeded.principle: DbView objects expose sub-objects (elements, expression filters, attribute filters, expression columns, attribute columns) that can be queried via !!CollectAllFor with type filter and $!dbView scope.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL'|'ATTFIL'|'EXPCOL'|'ATTCOL', ||, $!dbView) to collect DbView sub-objects scoped to a specific DbView instance.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Collect all EXPFIL under a DbView
!expList = !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL', ||, $!dbView)
do !exp values !expList
  !expr = !exp.Expression
  !type = !exp.ExpType
enddo
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- WRONG: Collecting EXPFIL without DbView scope
!badList = !!CollectAllFor('EXPFIL', ||, world) -- returns ALL EXPFIL in world, not scoped
pitfalls: Scope must use $!dbView reference, not just the DbView name
Each sub-object type has different attributes — check type-specific properties

newEntriesNeeded.title: DbView .elel property for element iteration
newEntriesNeeded.principle: DbView objects expose a .elel property that returns the list of elements included in the view.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Access !dbView.elel to iterate through elements of a DbView. Each element is a DBREF.
pitfalls: !ele is a DBREF, not a string — concatenate with string for CSV output

newEntriesNeeded.title: Handle NONE for var command recovery
newEntriesNeeded.principle: When a PML var command (like ATTDEF query) may fail due to missing or invalid references, wrap in handle none to provide a fallback value instead of aborting the macro.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use handle none (without error codes) when the var command is optional and a fallback value is acceptable. The handler assigns a default value to the variable.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
if (!condition) then
  var !result OBJECT $!<reference> ATTR1 ATTR2
  handle none
    !result = !defaultValue
  endhandle
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
if (!udName.unset() or !udName.empty()) then
  var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME TYPE RPTX SIZE DEFI DTYP UNIT VISI QSET QTXT ITYP DESTEX
  handle none
    !udName = !attData[3]
  endhandle
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- WRONG: handle any on optional var command
var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME
handle any
  !udName = !attData[3]
endhandle -- handle any catches ALL errors including programming mistakes
pitfalls: handle none catches ALL errors including typos — use only when fallback is intentional
var result array indexing (!attData[3]) depends on attribute order

newEntriesNeeded.title: NETDATASOURCE + NETGRIDCONTROL Excel export pattern
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE to create tabular data views and export to Excel. NETDATASOURCE takes a name, header array, and data array.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: 1) Create NETGRIDCONTROL object. 2) Create NETDATASOURCE with header list and data array. 3) Bind data source to grid. 4) Call saveGridToExcel with file path.
pitfalls: NETDATASOURCE constructor signature: (name, headers, data) — headers must be an ARRAY, data must be an ARRAY of arrays or strings
saveGridToExcel accepts file path as pipe-delimited string with $! variable substitution
import 'GridControl' with handle ANY tolerance is recommended — NETGRIDCONTROL may not be available in all environments

newEntriesNeeded.title: String .unset() and .empty() methods
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML string objects provide .unset() and .empty() methods for validation. .unset() checks if the variable is unset/BADREF. .empty() checks if the string is empty or whitespace.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use !str.unset() to check BADREF/unset state. Use !str.empty() to check for empty/whitespace content. Combine with .or() for guard conditions.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
if (!str.unset() or !str.empty()) then
  -- handle missing or empty value
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
if (!udName.unset() or !udName.empty()) then
  var !attData ATTDEF $!<att.DbAttribute> NAME TYPE RPTX SIZE DEFI DTYP UNIT VISI QSET QTXT ITYP DESTEX
  handle none
    !udName = !attData[3]
  endhandle
endif
pitfalls: .unset() returns TRUE if the variable is BADREF or never assigned
.empty() returns TRUE for empty strings and whitespace-only strings
